Can you study in the UK without IELTS in 2027? Yes. IELTS is widely recognised, but it is not the only evidence of English proficiency that UK universities consider. Depending on your course and background, you may qualify through a different English test, a previous qualification taught in English, a Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate or a university assessment.

The important word is depending. A university might accept Duolingo for one course but not another. An MOI letter may work for a recent graduate yet be insufficient for someone who completed their degree years ago. And an offer of admission does not remove other requirements that apply to international students.

This guide explains the realistic options for January and September 2027 entry, compares universities that publish IELTS alternatives and shows you what to check before paying for another test. It focuses on academic admission, where each university has the final say on acceptable evidence.

Can You Study in the UK Without IELTS in 2027?

The short answer is yes, provided your chosen university accepts other evidence that meets its English-language standard. Without IELTS does not mean without English proficiency. You still need sufficient reading, writing, listening and speaking skills to succeed in lectures, seminars and assessments.

Most universities express their requirements as an IELTS score or its equivalent. A course asking for IELTS 6.0, for example, may publish corresponding scores for PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT or Duolingo. Another institution might accept an approved school English qualification or an English-taught degree instead.

The safest starting point is your specific course page, not a generic list of universities said to offer IELTS-free admission. For a broader explanation of how universities assess language ability, see the different forms of English evidence used for UK entry.

Five Ways to Study in the UK Without IELTS

1. Use a Medium of Instruction certificate

An MOI certificate confirms that your previous programme was taught and assessed in English. Some universities consider this evidence for selected applicants, particularly graduates applying for a master's degree. Acceptance depends on your institution, country, qualification, graduation date and chosen programme.

For instance, the University of Southampton may consider an undergraduate degree taught and assessed in English. Its evidence rules differ for degrees completed within two years and those completed two to five years before the intended start date. MOI is therefore a potential route, not an automatic exemption.

2. Present an accepted school or university qualification

Some universities recognise English results from particular national qualifications. This can be more useful than an MOI letter for an undergraduate applicant who has not yet completed a degree. Accepted qualifications vary by country and university, and certain professional courses impose stricter rules.

3. Take another recognised English test

PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, Duolingo English Test, LanguageCert, Cambridge English and Oxford ELLT can be alternatives where a university expressly accepts them. They are not interchangeable. The institution may specify a test-centre version, an overall score and minimum marks in all four skills.

4. Complete a university English assessment

Some universities offer their own assessment. Birmingham City University, for example, publishes information about its English Proficiency Test. A university's internal assessment is generally intended for its own admissions process, so do not assume another institution will accept the result.

5. Consider a pre-sessional English course

A pre-sessional programme helps applicants whose English is below the direct-entry requirement. It takes additional time and may involve a separate fee, but it can be more appropriate than repeatedly sitting an unsuitable test. Check the entry requirements for the pre-sessional course itself before applying.

Here's the thing: an existing qualification that your university already recognises can be more useful than a new, cheaper online test that it does not accept. Start with what you have, then identify what is missing.

UK Universities Without IELTS in 2027: Options to Check

There is no reliable universal list of UK universities that waive IELTS for every applicant. The institutions below publish other ways to demonstrate English ability. They are examples of possible routes, not promises of admission for 2027. Always check the current course requirements and any nationality restrictions.

Its standard IELTS 6.0 equivalency includes Duolingo 105 and Pearson 64, with minimum skill scores and course exceptions.

Bangor University

For an IELTS 6.0 (5.5) profile, published examples include Duolingo 105 and Oxford ELLT 6 (5). Sub-scores matter.

Duolingo is restricted to nationals covered by the university's stated eligibility rule. Some professional courses have exceptions.

Duolingo and Oxford ELLT are not currently accepted for direct degree entry; PTE Academic Online is also excluded.

PTE, TOEFL, Cambridge English and Duolingo among its listed routes

Some qualifications trigger an additional English or credibility interview. Course-specific restrictions apply.

Robert Gordon University

Most taught postgraduate courses normally require an IELTS-equivalent 6.5, although individual courses differ.

Recent degrees taught and assessed in English, plus recognised English qualifications

The age of the degree and evidence of English-language study or recent professional use affect assessment.

Selected national qualifications and conditional MOI evidence

Its published Pakistan MOI route is limited to qualifying four-year degrees from named institutions and assessed case by case.

How to use this list: shortlist universities for your subject, open each course's English requirements and ask admissions to confirm whether your exact qualification, test version and country are acceptable. A university may list a test for pre-sessional English but reject it for direct degree entry. Written confirmation is more useful than a general statement that a university is “IELTS-free”.

Can You Use an MOI Certificate Instead of IELTS?

Potentially. An MOI letter normally comes from the institution where you completed your previous qualification. It should clearly identify you, name your qualification, give your study dates and confirm that the programme was taught and assessed in English. A letter saying merely that your college uses English may not be enough.

Consider two master's applicants. One completed an English-taught degree last year and has a detailed MOI letter. The other graduated six years ago with a brief letter that says only “medium: English”. They should not expect the same decision, even if their academic marks are identical.

Southampton's published policy for English-taught degrees illustrates why recency matters: certain degrees completed within two years may be supported by academic documents, while degrees completed two to five years earlier require additional evidence, such as suitable recent professional use of English or an approved test. For more institution-specific conditions, compare universities that evaluate previous English-medium study.

Do not assume an MOI certificate independently meets every requirement outside university admission. The receiving institution must decide whether it is acceptable for the programme and applicant.

IELTS Alternatives Accepted by UK Universities

Choosing the right test is less about finding the easiest exam and more about matching your course's evidence rules.

What to check first

For example, Sheffield Hallam lists Duolingo 105 alongside Pearson 64 for its standard IELTS 6.0 equivalency, whereas Chester's acceptance of Duolingo is subject to nationality restrictions. The numbers alone cannot tell you whether either route works for you.

Another detail is easy to miss: TOEFL iBT introduced a new 1 to 6 score scale in January 2026. Universities now publish requirements for results taken before and after that change. Check the date on your result, not just the overall number.

If you are choosing between test providers, you can compare where Pearson scores are recognised for degree admission, which courses consider the online Duolingo test and how institutions assess Oxford ELLT results. These specialist lists provide detail without turning this guide into three separate test directories.

Does Admission Without IELTS Settle Other English Requirements?

Undergraduate and Master's Study Without IELTS

Master's applicants may have more evidence available because they have already completed a degree. Some universities consider a recent English-taught qualification or MOI letter; others require an approved English test regardless. Research degrees and courses leading to professional registration may have additional conditions.

Undergraduate applicants are more likely to rely on school-level English qualifications, PTE, TOEFL, Duolingo or another recognised assessment. A university might accept a national school English grade for one applicant but request a separate test from another.

For both levels, the course takes priority over the university's general table. Nursing, medicine, pharmacy, social work and teacher training can impose higher language standards. Check the programme's entry page and any relevant professional requirements before choosing your English route.

Can Students from Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Nepal or Nigeria Apply Without IELTS?

Yes, where the university accepts their individual English evidence. Nationality does not provide a blanket IELTS waiver. The differences are practical and sometimes substantial.

Bangladesh: Applicants may have MOI or other evidence considered at selected institutions, but restrictions matter. Greenwich specifically excludes Bangladeshi nationals from using Oxford ELLT as its IELTS waiver. Do not assume a test offered to applicants elsewhere will be available on identical terms.

India: Some universities recognise English results from specific Class XII boards. Birmingham City University, for instance, lists 65% for selected boards when a course requires IELTS 6.0, with higher thresholds for higher course requirements. It is not an automatic exemption for every board or programme.

Pakistan: A recognised English-medium degree may create an MOI route. Nottingham Trent, however, limits its published case-by-case option to specified institutions and qualifying four-year bachelor's degrees. The awarding university matters as much as the wording of the letter.

Nepal: Birmingham City University publishes a route using Nepal Grade XII English, including 65% or Grade B for courses requiring IELTS 6.0, normally with its own listening and speaking assessment. A higher school result can change that additional assessment requirement. Check the exact conditions rather than relying on the school mark alone.

Nigeria: Recognised WAEC or NECO English grades may be accepted at selected universities. Birmingham City University lists C6 for programmes with a standard IELTS 6.0 requirement, while courses requiring IELTS 6.5 need the higher C5 grade.

A recurring admissions mistake is to copy an online success story without checking the applicant's course, nationality or graduation date. Two students applying to the same university can legitimately receive different English-language conditions.

January and September 2027 Entry: When Should You Apply?

January 2027 may suit applicants who already have suitable academic documents and English evidence. Not every course offers a January start, and some English preparation programmes begin months before the degree. First check the programme's availability, then its actual deadline and entry conditions. You can narrow your search through UK courses with an early-year start.

September 2027 generally offers a broader selection of courses and more time to resolve an English-language condition. For many undergraduate courses, the UCAS equal-consideration deadline for 2027 entry is 13 January 2027; certain courses and institutions have earlier deadlines. You can compare autumn-entry options and their published timelines before deciding when to apply.

A useful sequence is to choose the course, verify the English evidence it accepts and only then commit to a test date or application timetable.

How Much Does It Cost to Study in the UK Without IELTS?

Avoiding IELTS may save the price of that particular test, but it does not reduce tuition fees or living costs automatically. If your existing qualification is accepted, your additional English-test cost could be £0. If you need PTE, TOEFL, Duolingo or a pre-sessional course, the cost will depend on the provider and route.

For context, UCAS estimates international tuition at approximately £22,000 a year for undergraduate study and £17,109 a year for postgraduate study on average. These are broad published estimates, not guaranteed 2027 course fees. The 2027 UCAS undergraduate application fee is £34.50 for up to five choices.

A specific example is more useful than an unsupported national average. The University of Portsmouth lists £18,600 for international full-time students on its MA International Relations starting in January 2027. It has not yet confirmed that course's September 2027 international fee on the same page.

Scholarships may improve affordability, but they have separate eligibility and award conditions. Bangor University publishes a competitive £10,000 Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship for eligible 2027 undergraduate and taught postgraduate entrants, with limited awards. Portsmouth lists a £2,500 first-year fee reduction for eligible January 2027 entrants from countries including Bangladesh, India, Nepal, Nigeria and Pakistan. Its published conditions include full-time on-campus study and annual course fees of at least £16,200.

Neither scholarship should be treated as guaranteed, and neither changes the English requirement for the chosen course. Compare the final course fee and official award conditions first. If affordability is central to your choice, examine lower-fee university options separately from English-test eligibility.

How to Apply to UK Universities Without IELTS

Begin with the degree you want, rather than the exam you hope to avoid. Read the course page, identify the English requirement and compare it with your available evidence.

If you studied in English, obtain a properly worded MOI letter or other recognised academic record. If you have school-level English results, check whether your target university recognises your board and grades. If neither works, select an alternative test that the university explicitly accepts, including the correct test format and minimum component scores.

Then gather your academic certificates, transcripts, English evidence and any course-specific material such as references, a personal statement or portfolio. Undergraduate applicants using UCAS should follow the application stages and supporting-document rules; taught postgraduate courses often have their own university application processes.

Submit the academic application, monitor any conditions in your offer and ask the university about anything unclear. In particular, confirm that your English evidence meets the exact programme requirement before paying a substantial non-refundable charge.

FAQs About Studying in the UK Without IELTS

Can I study in the UK without IELTS in 2027?

Yes. Some UK universities accept approved English qualifications, alternative tests, MOI evidence or their own assessments. You must still meet the English requirement for your course.

Which UK universities accept students without IELTS?

Greenwich, Sheffield Hallam, Bangor, Chester, Birmingham City, Portsmouth, Robert Gordon, Southampton and Nottingham Trent publish various IELTS alternatives or conditional routes. None offers an unconditional waiver for every applicant.

Can I apply to UK universities without taking any English test?

Possibly, if the university accepts a previous English-taught qualification, a suitable MOI certificate or an eligible school English result. The admissions team must confirm that your evidence meets the course's standard.

Is an MOI certificate accepted for a UK master's degree?

At selected universities and for qualifying applicants, yes. Your institution, course, country and graduation date can affect acceptance. An MOI letter alone is not a universal exemption.

Can I use PTE instead of IELTS for UK university admission?

Many universities accept PTE Academic, but minimum overall and skill scores differ. Some universities do not accept its online version. Always check the exact qualification listed on your course page.

Is Duolingo accepted by UK universities in 2027?

Selected institutions publish Duolingo equivalencies. Acceptance may depend on nationality, course and an interview. Chester and Portsmouth, for example, publish additional conditions.

Can Bangladeshi students study in the UK without IELTS?

Yes, where a university accepts their alternative English evidence. However, options differ across institutions. For example, Greenwich does not permit Bangladeshi nationals to use Oxford ELLT as an IELTS waiver, so applicants should check nationality-specific conditions directly.

Can I study a master's degree without IELTS?

Yes, if your programme recognises suitable alternative evidence. A recent degree taught and assessed in English may help, but some programmes insist on a particular approved test or higher English standard.

Are there UK universities without IELTS and application fees?

Some universities allow eligible direct applications without a separate institutional application charge. That does not mean every course is free to apply to. UCAS charges £34.50 for up to five undergraduate choices in the 2027 cycle, unless an applicable waiver is available.

Can I get a scholarship without IELTS?

Final Thoughts

Studying in the UK without IELTS in 2027 is possible when you match the right English evidence to the right course. A recognised school qualification, an eligible English-taught degree, MOI or an accepted alternative test may be enough for academic admission. None is a universal waiver, and a test offered for a pre-sessional course may not qualify you for direct degree entry.

Choose the subject and institution first. Verify the current course policy, including test formats, nationality restrictions and minimum scores in each skill. Then compare the January or September 2027 start date, tuition fees and scholarship conditions. Often, the best way to avoid an unnecessary English test is simply to check whether your existing evidence is already acceptable.

If you would like to compare suitable courses and discuss the academic application process, contact our university admissions team. You can explore your options without assuming any institution will grant an IELTS waiver. The university always makes the final admission decision.
